identity.name: Chinese Communists (Jinggangshan and Jiangxi soviet bases)

land.text: the Jinggang Mountains on the Jiangxi-Hunan border, where Mao Zedong's group 'established a base in the remote Jinggang Mountains'

predecessors.note: A rebel base inside Nationalist China; the page does not date the founding (Cliopatria: 1928).

land.text: the Jiangxi-Fujian soviet area around Ruijin, where the Chinese Soviet Republic was proclaimed on 7 November 1931

successors.note: Cliopatria's next row (Communist Party of China) starts in 1932. Both rows carry Wikidata Q17427 and are one party-state continuing; kept as two dossiers because the second belongs to another batch.

capitals.name: Ruijin
capitals.note: Capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic from its proclamation in November 1931; the earlier base in the Jinggang Mountains has no named seat on the pages.

keyframe_review.note: 38,942 km2 for 1928-29, bbox 113.6-115.3 E, 25.7-29.0 N: the Jinggang Mountains base on the Jiangxi-Hunan border. The pages give neither a date nor an area for it ('A large group in southern China commanded by Mao Zedong established a base in the remote Jinggang Mountains'); the only area on the pages is about 70,000 km2 for the Chinese Soviet Republic in 1933, within a factor of two of this shape plus the later Ruijin zone. Unverified: page budget.

union.text: Ruijin and the border region between Jiangxi and Fujian, the later seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic

correction.text: the 1930 shape plus the Jiangxi-Fujian border region around Ruijin

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria repeats the 1928 shape for 1930-31. The page says a Kuomintang campaign forced Mao's group 'into the border region between Jiangxi and Fujian provinces' and that 'Beginning in 1929, soviets began to be created in isolated regions across the country'; Ruijin (116.0 E) lies outside the shape's bbox, yet the Soviet Republic was proclaimed there in November 1931. Ruijin and its radius are added; the dates of the move are not on the page.

region.text: the Jinggang Mountains base on the Jiangxi-Hunan border

ledger.note: 1928: the Communists hold a base in the Jinggang Mountains. The Jinggangshan page opened (a disambiguation page) is silent, and this page says only that Mao's group 'established a base in the remote Jinggang Mountains' without a date; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Ruijin and the border region between Jiangxi and Fujian, the later seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic

ledger.note: 1930: the Communists extend to the Jiangxi-Fujian border around Ruijin. 'a Kuomintang campaign forced Mao's group into the border region between Jiangxi and Fujian provinces'; 'Beginning in 1929, soviets began to be created in isolated regions'. The pages are silent on the year of the move; the year is bridged from Cliopatria's 1930 row.

union.text: Ruijin and the border region between Jiangxi and Fujian, the later seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic

region.text: the soviet bases of Jiangxi, Hunan and Fujian, now the Chinese Soviet Republic

ledger.note: 1931: the Chinese Soviet Republic is proclaimed at Ruijin on 7 November. 'proclaimed on 7 November 1931 by Chinese Communist Party (CCP) leaders Mao Zedong and Zhu De'; 'In November 1931, a National Soviet People's Delegates Conference proclaimed the CSR in Ruijin, Jiangxi.' The Soviet Republic is the next Cliopatria row (Communist Party of China, 1932-1949).

wars.name: Encirclement campaigns against the Jiangxi Soviet
wars.outcome: The Soviet 'survived the first, second and third encirclement campaigns thanks to the use of flexible guerrilla tactics'; the fifth campaign (1933) and the fall of Ruijin (10 November 1934) belong to the next dossier.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the first campaigns (the first in December 1930, the second in 1931 are not on the page) and no land that changed hands, so the zones are empty.

certainty.note: Guerrilla bases in the mountains: the pages give no boundary at all; Ruijin and the Jinggang Mountains are the only points.

sources.title: Chinese Soviet Republic
sources.note: Founding 7 November 1931 at Ruijin; the Jinggang Mountains base and the Jiangxi-Fujian border region (undated); 1933 area about 70,000 km2.

notes: Page budget (1-2) spent: the Jinggangshan page was a disambiguation page and the Chinese Soviet Republic page is thin on 1927-1931. Nothing on the pages dates the Jinggangshan base, Zhu De's arrival or the January 1929 withdrawal, the Gutian conference, or the encirclement campaigns; a gap-filler should open 'Jinggang Mountains', 'Jiangxi Soviet' and 'Encirclement campaigns against the Jiangxi Soviet'. Q17427 is shared with communist-party-of-china (1932-1949). They are one continuing party-state; I keep two dossiers because the second is owned by another batch of this group and this brief says not to touch it. The colour agent should treat them as one colour family (china), and the second dossier should list this one as its predecessor. Gazetteer: no place entry for Ruijin (a coordinate is used). The Nationalist government is counterpart kuomintang to 1929 and republic-of-china from 1930, as Cliopatria's neighbours list has it.
